reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds on record.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, so I'll check the orders next to confirm the refunds apply correctly before paying anyone.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and both refunds are smaller than their orders, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 36083 matches its two orders (18974 + 17109) with no refunds, so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which should reflect refund 234.

Birch's net of 28695 matches its orders (21055 + 11644 = 32699) minus refund 234 (4004), so it checks out. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net should reflect refund 235 (orders 14171 + 16756 = 30927, minus 1660 = 29267), so I'll fetch it now.
All three net balances match the orders minus refunds, and the refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so I'll record the payouts. Starting with acme at 36083.
Acme's payout of 36083 is recorded. Birch's net balance of 28695 already matched its orders minus refund 234, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 29267 matches orders 14171 + 16756 minus refund 235 (1660), so I'll record its payout now to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each amount matched net_balance and was checked against orders minus refunds. The batch is complete.
